5687.name: Southern Guard's Walk, West Wall
5687.description: This, the west wall, is in the most danger of assault, and everyone who has ever held the castle has known it. It faces the sea, and no commander worth the name would come at Tordraken by land when a hull can be laid alongside the cliff foot on a calm day. Having foreseen this, whoever designed the castle allowed for large arrow slots to be built into the wall, and whoever came after put teeth behind them: a ballista stands to every third slot on a timber turntable, cranked back and pegged, its bolt-tray dry under oiled canvas. Through the wide slots the grey run of the water is visible all the way out. The hall continues north, and to the south is an iron door.

5781.name: Northern Guard's Walk, West Wall 2nd Floor
5781.description: Sneaking in through tiny cracks around the edges of the arrow hatches, a wet draught crawls down the hall, and it carries salt with it — every iron fitting on this side wears a rind of rust the armourers scrape off and lose again. The constant hissing and whistling grows increasingly louder as the wind picks up. Many of the torches have gone out in this area, leaving it dark and unattended. Pieces of ceiling are beginning to crumble and fall away, exposing the understone that makes up the framework of the castle. To the south the guard's walk continues, and an iron door leads north.

5706.name: A Cold Viewing Chamber
5706.description: The walls here are lined with a second skin of dressed stone, and a drain runs in the floor for the water that beads off it. The room is kept cold on purpose: an undercroft chill, carried up from the cliff by a shaft in the north wall, holds the case that stands there. The case is glass and lead over a bath of clear brine, and in it lies the body of a woman, perhaps in her early thirties. Her features are soft and subtle, though a force of undeniable malevolence dwells beneath the surface of her beauty. She has a magnificent golden mane of hair that wraps over her right shoulder and rests on her breastplate. She wears a full suit of sparkling blue earthstone armour that covers her from neck to toe, full plate in style, allowing maximum movement for minimum weight. The trim and plate edges are white, and a dragon's head is worked on the breast. The gauntlets are made from the scales of a sea-drake, dyed blue and white; the boots are thick sealskin plated with the same. There is no helm and no shield, and no weapon — it does not look as though she was laid down with any of them. The only exit is to the south.

78225.name: A Portcullis Slams Shut Behind You!
78225.description: The walls of the vault are the raw stone of the headland, cut and left, as though the room were not part of the castle at all but a hollow the castle was built to cover. No dressed face can be seen anywhere. It is very cold, and breath shows. Statues and sculptures line the walls, each of various women performing some horrid act of violence, and each one carved from the same wet- looking rock. There are shelves cut into the stone on all of the walls except the north, which houses the door. An uncountable number of little trinkets lines the floor and the shelves; it would take days to sort through them all, and somebody clearly once tried.

5729.name: North End, East Wing Of the Banquet Hall
5729.description: A plaque on the wall to the north clearly stakes claim to this table. A large device has been scratched into the centre of the boards, proudly claiming it as though the plaque were not enough: the dragon's head of the house, with two jagged spears crossed underneath it. Other than the vandalism the table is very well kept and quite clean. Towards the centre of the room a hot fire burns in a lowered section of the floor, and the smoke goes up and out through a flue that moans when the wind is in the west. To the south and the west lie more tables.

5725.name: The Head Table of the Banquet Hall
5725.description: The head table is much like the others except larger, and without the black surface. The top is bluish earthstone with a dragon's head inlaid in white at the centre. There is no food on it, just the remains of a hare. Someone has traced the inlay with the blood of the hare, following the lines carefully, all the way round. A large white goblet with blue trim is the only dish. A small serrated knife lies next to the carcass. The chair behind the table is modelled from a human hand: it comes up out of the stone of the floor, the palm forming the seat while the fingers curve up and over to make the backrest.

5815.name: The Duchess's Private Office
5815.description: This is the private office of Strife, who holds Tordraken and styles herself its Duchess. A small shrine carved from ivory is inset into the north wall behind the wide pale desk — a detailed temple with a cathedral ceiling, a raised dais, an altar upon it and numerous tiny carved figures standing about the scene, all of them facing the same way. The desk is well made, thin-framed with a black slate top for a smooth surface. There are no cabinets here, only the desk, a nondescript chair, and a sinfully comfortable, fur-lined sofa. It is really more of a chair, but strange in that it is very deep: one sinks in and is surrounded. The only exit is to the south, entering on a massive round table.

5812.name: Southwestern Section of a Massive Round Table
5812.description: The ceiling rises to a higher level here, and the room seems to extend for some distance to the east and north. Several doors can be seen a way off to the north, set equidistantly along the wall. A huge sheet of rock that must be sixty feet long rests atop large blocks of stone, forming a massive round table, its surface ground smooth and slightly polished for use. Surrounding it are large gothic chairs with high backs and soft red cushions. In the centre of the table, firmly anchored to the stone, a crystal the size of a fist glows quietly from the inside. The light is pleasantly dim, provided by candelabra suspended from the ceiling with reflectors that keep the upper half of the room in shadow. The room feels very neutral; the air does not seem to move, and there is not a sound from anywhere. Silken banners of blue and grey hang in shadow on the wall, displaying the dragon's head. The round table continues to the north and east, and a small hall leads west.

5820.name: Southern Side of a Massive Round Table
5820.description: This spot is directly across from the head of the table. The position is not as prestigious as the one opposite, but it is more important than those surrounding it, and the chair is raised higher than its neighbours — though not as high as the alabaster seat at the head. The table here is dominated by a great chart of the headland. The castle sits at the centre of it, and the road up the cliff runs through the southern portion. Off to the east a path leads up through a narrow pass between two peaks; below them, past the trail, lies the deep vale the cataract runs down on its way to the sea. Soundings are marked all along the western edge in a careful hand, and the places a hull could stand in close are ringed twice. The round table continues to the east and west.

15780.name: Tactical Room of the Guard's Upper Echelon
15780.description: This chamber is a war room high in the guard tower of Tordraken Castle. The walls are lined with large wooden racks holding scrolls and rolled parchment charts of the surrounding coast and the strategic points along it. A long, sturdy oak table stands at the centre, covered in further charts and notes scattered about, indicating recent planning. The floor is cold underfoot from the constant draught that comes through the gaps between the stones near the ceiling, where a slit has been left open for ventilation and for the look-out's voice. Iron braziers along the walls give a dim glow and do little against the damp that comes in off the water.

5807.name: The Midpoint of an Elegant Marble Gallery
5807.description: This is almost the perfect geometric centre of the castle's upper floor, and the halfway point in the gallery, which stems off the north-south guard's walk very near the middle. The red carpet covers the entire floor here, leaving just the edges of the marble showing at the base of the walls. Empty suits of plate armour stand against the south and north walls, each bearing a smouldering brazier in its hands. The scented smoke drifts up towards the ceiling where it mixes with the torch smoke from the rest of the gallery. Hanging from the ceiling, unstained by the pitch, a blue silk banner with the dragon's head at its centre provides the only artistic decoration the hall has to offer. The gallery continues to the east and west, and a velvet covered staircase lies to the north.

78794.name: A Balcony Overlooking the Castle Entrance
78794.description: The roof of the castle extends over this outdoor balcony, providing shelter from the rain that arrives here horizontally more often than not. The balcony is much like the guard's walk, empty and devoid of decoration. A half wall provides a barrier from falling off the edge into the turbulent cleft below, where the sea works. The immaculate road leading south towards the edge of the Tordraken cliffs can be seen all the way to its end, cutting the cropped headland grass in two. The land drops away into what looks like a vale at the far southern edge of the cliffs, past where the road begins. The western edge is a few minutes' walk from the road and then nothing at all for a very long way, and to the east the headland runs on until the hills rise higher than the cliff's own surface. The balcony continues to the west, and an iron door leads east.

78795.name: Midpoint In the Balcony Overlooking the Castle Entrance
78795.description: At this point the balcony stands directly above the castle entrance. Below, the span of the bridge can be seen, dark with spray and shining where the light finds the wet. From here the surroundings take on a different character: out of the wind, with the noise of the water arriving a moment late, the landscape is allowed to be fantastic rather than merely hostile. The country below the cliffs is not directly visible, but the green of it comes up as a suggestion in the haze and brings a little warmth to the scene. The balcony continues to the east and west.
